existing_art.what: Hip prosthesis failure prediction, radiographic deep sequence learning, 1454 patients, external validation
existing_art.implication: AI implant failure prediction with external validation ALREADY EXISTS

existing_art.what: Shunt complication prediction, 33,248 patients, ROC AUC 0.733, independently validated
existing_art.implication: AI shunt failure prediction ALREADY EXISTS and is validated
Patent landscape already contemplates AI/ML in shunts

differentiators.test: Is on-device prediction materially better than cloud for any clinical scenario?
differentiators.rationale: Most implant monitoring already uses cloud upload. On-device is a feature, not a moat.
differentiators.published_evidence: Cloud-based implant monitoring is standard (Medtronic CareLink, Abbott Merlin.net)

differentiators.test: Does neuromorphic enable prediction at <1mW where conventional ML cannot?
differentiators.rationale: IF power budget is truly constraining (<100μW), neuromorphic may be the only option. Depends on P-15/P-16 energy results.
differentiators.published_evidence: Intel Loihi 2: ~1W typical. Not yet <1mW for real prediction tasks. SpiNNaker: similar. Neuromorphic hardware is NOT yet at implantable power levels.
differentiators.conditional_on: P-15 (cardiac harvesting) or P-16 (NIR PV) must provide enough power for a neuromorphic chip

differentiators.test: Does continuous event-driven sensing detect failure earlier than periodic cloud upload?
differentiators.rationale: IF failure develops over minutes (not hours/days), continuous matters. But most implant failures develop over days-weeks.
differentiators.published_evidence: Shunt failure typically develops over hours-days. Cardiac device failure can be minutes-hours. Application-dependent.

differentiators.test: Is there a clinical/regulatory scenario where data cannot leave the device?
differentiators.rationale: HIPAA-compliant cloud upload is standard practice. No clinical scenario currently requires on-device-only processing.
differentiators.published_evidence: FDA allows cloud-connected implantable devices with proper cybersecurity (FDA guidance 2018)

differentiators.test: Is there a clinical scenario where patient has no connectivity for extended periods?
differentiators.rationale: Most patients in developed markets have connectivity. Rural/developing markets may benefit, but this is a niche.
differentiators.published_evidence: Medtronic CareLink requires periodic connectivity but buffers data locally

conditional_on: P-15 or P-16 must provide enough power for neuromorphic chip
limitations: Neuromorphic hardware not at implantable power
